newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian MTBE - Steady, trade winds down ahead of hols.
newsitem.headline: Asian MTBE - Steady, trade winds down ahead of hols.

text.p: Spot Asian MTBE prices were steady at firm levels amid tight supplies but in lacklustre trade ahead of holidays in February, traders said on Wednesday.
"There was none for this week," a producer said, describing the trading activity.
Trade in the region had slowed down ahead on Lunar New Year and the Eid-el-Fitri celebrations starting this weekend, traders said.
"Everybody is wrapping up before the holiday," said another producer. "There are only some small enquiries from Indonesia and Thailand, but there is a slight tightness."
A Mideast supplier maintained offers at $280-$289 per tonne on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) Singapore basis, while free-on-board parcels were notional around $270-$275.
As supplies for February were already committed, traders started to look towards March but Malaysia was already heard sold out, having moved large quantities to the U.S.

Traders expected prices in March to hold steady on the back of firm Asian gasoline prices or soften slightly with cheaper feedstock prices and the official start-up of the 700,000-tonne per year Saudi MTBE plant in February.
But an industry source, however, said the destination of supplies from the new plant had not yet been decided.
Although there has been no reduction in MTBE requirements for blenders, Taiwan's recent tender results were disappointing, traders said.
High offers limited Taiwan's purchase to one 250,000-barrel cargo of reformate with a two percent MTBE requirement for March 1-15 arrival, eventhough it was seeking at least two cargoes.
It paid a record $27.60 per barrel c-and-f Taiwan, but said would emerge after the Lunar New Year to buy more March cargoes.
Prices for MTBE feedstock, methanol were also expected to soften by the end of the first quarter and then stabilise, a supplier said.
Methanol prices had already stopped their upward trend and were steady at $235-$240 per tonne this week, compared to hikes of nearly $90 in recent weeks.
Feedstock supplies have improved with the return of Malaysia state-owned Petronas Methanol Labuan's 660,000-tonne-per-year plant on February 3, albeit only operating at 85-90 percent.
The East Malaysian plant was shutdown on December 26 when storms damaged a boiler.
Although the replacement boiler is ready, Petronas is postponing the 30-35 day shutdown required for the process until July.
"We have to first replace inventory and build up stocks because term cargo liftings have been deferred," a company source said.
